payload.meta_description: Australia has no marriage licence. The legal step is the Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM): when to lodge it, documents, fees and marrying overseas.
payload.excerpt: Australia issues no marriage licence. Here is how the Notice of Intended Marriage works, who can witness it at home or abroad, what each state charges for your certificate, and how to plan if you marry overseas.

key_takeaways: Australia does not issue a marriage licence: the legal step is the Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM), given to your authorised celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.

Since 12 June 2024 a NOIM can be witnessed by video link inside Australia; if you are overseas, the safe route is to sign in person before an authorised witness where you are, such as a notary public or an Australian consular officer.
On the day, your celebrant, both of you and two witnesses over 18 must all be physically present, and three marriage certificates are signed.

The certificate your celebrant hands you is ceremonial; the one you use for a passport or bank is ordered from the registry in the state where you married, from AUD 58.10 in Queensland to AUD 74 in the Northern Territory (fees checked November 2026; ACT fee not published here).
A marriage overseas is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid here, but it cannot be registered in Australia.

faq.q: Do you need a marriage licence to get married in Australia?
faq.a: No. Australia does not issue a marriage licence. The legal step is the Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM), which you both sign and give to your authorised celebrant at least one month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.

faq.q: How long does it take to get legally married in Australia?
faq.a: At least one month from giving your NOIM to your celebrant, unless a prescribed authority (the official your celebrant can point you to) agrees to shorten that period. Approval is not automatic, so talk to your celebrant first.

faq.q: What paperwork is needed to get married in Australia?
faq.a: The NOIM, evidence of each partner's date and place of birth (a birth certificate or passport), photo identification, and, if either of you was married before, evidence that the marriage ended. Before the ceremony you each sign a Declaration of No Legal Impediment to Marriage, and on the day three marriage certificates are signed.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a marriage certificate in Australia?
faq.a: Your celebrant has 14 days to lodge the paperwork. Then NSW quotes up to three weeks for online orders, Queensland up to 10 business days and Western Australia up to two working days, each plus postage; check your own registry's page.

faq.q: How much does it cost to marry legally in Australia?
faq.a: The official fee is for the registry marriage certificate, for example AUD 70 in NSW and AUD 59.10 in Victoria (both from 1 July 2026) and AUD 58.10 in Queensland (November 2026). The table in this guide lists every state. Your celebrant's fee is separate, so ask for it in writing.

faq.q: Can we sign the NOIM if one of us is overseas?
faq.a: Yes. The partner overseas signs in person before an authorised witness there, such as an Australian consular or diplomatic officer or a notary public. AGD says a NOIM for someone outside Australia cannot be witnessed online, so an Australian celebrant cannot witness it by video call.
